name: A Net Disaster

angles.text: As an Alliance traveler, you find Crystal Lake in Elwynn Forest. Disruptions there threaten local livelihoods and the supplies that support Alliance territory.

faq.answer: At Crystal Lake in Elwynn Forest, fishermen find no fish on their hooks and no minnows in the shallows. They set traps overnight to protect their stock.
Lee's overnight fishing traps lie beneath the waters of Crystal Lake. Lee set them to preserve the fish stock after hook-and-line fishing failed.
faq.q: Where do you inspect the fishing traps?

faq.answer: Lee is a fisherman at Crystal Lake. After hook-and-line fishing brought in nothing, Lee set traps overnight to secure the fish stock.

aliases: what happened to crystal lake fish
faq.answer: No fish are biting, and not even minnows appear in Crystal Lake's shallows. Hostile neighbors have ruined the overnight traps.
faq.q: What happened to the fish in Crystal Lake?

faq.answer: The neighboring nuisances are aggressive murlocs. They have made camps in Crystal Lake's waters and along its shores, disrupting local wildlife and fishing gear.
faq.q: Who are the neighboring nuisances mentioned at the end?

aliases: why does the quest giver care
faq.answer: The fishermen rely on Crystal Lake's fish for their livelihoods. With the catch gone and the traps ruined, their work and income are at risk.
faq.q: Why is the lack of fish such a big problem for the fishermen?

sections.body: Fishermen at Crystal Lake in Elwynn Forest come up empty. Hooks bring in no fish, and even the minnows have vanished from the shallows. So they set traps overnight, hoping to catch enough to keep their stock.
sections.title: Troubled Waters at Crystal Lake

sections.body: Lee's traps beneath Crystal Lake lie ruined. Hostile neighbors along the shore have wrecked the fishing gear. If the damage continues, local fishermen risk losing their livelihoods.
sections.title: Wrecked Traps and Neighboring Nuisances

summary: At Crystal Lake, A Net Disaster starts with fishermen finding no fish on their hooks and no minnows in the shallows. They set traps overnight to protect their stock.
